I see. I was just confused by the use of the word "intuition", which to me typically means a simple and easily understandable logical explanation or analogy like "what's the intuition for why airplanes can fly?" 

In this case, your "intuition" seems to be your back of the envelope estimate on how much we should expect AI development/research to accelerate due to RSI. I don't even disagree with the 50x or 5x numbers. These are your guestimates, which are as good as anyone's. 

I just don't see any attempt at intuitive explanation for why 50x/5x should be the right numbers except "some studies showed AI is 50x faster at some tasks" plus a bit of handwaving on diminishing marginal returns to get us to 5x.

If you look at my tweet below from 2019, you’ll see that I recommended buying Bitcoin at around $3,600. The same process that told me to buy Bitcoin back then is now telling me that we’ve probably seen the end of Bitcoin’s bull story.

Could I be wrong? Of course. I give it a 50% chance that Bitcoin makes new highs and a 50% chance that it never does.

Bitcoin had its chance. Since I recommended buying it in 2019, it has failed at pretty much everything besides appreciating in price. It never became a practical payment system. Today, you have leveraged financial products that give you exposure without even owning Bitcoin. And after all that, we’re back around the same price as five years ago.

Bitcoin has existed for almost 18 years and has spent the last five going nowhere. Why are you so convinced it’s guaranteed to keep going up?

It failed the tests of inflation, Fed policy, money supply and being a store of value. It behaves like a risk asset, not the revolutionary currency we were promised.

You can invent patterns, call it a bear market, talk about cycles, but the only thing you’re really clinging to is hope.

I prefer to put my money where I see a better investment case. If Elon Musk is right about what SpaceX can accomplish, perhaps there’s an opportunity to make 5 to 10 times your money over the next decade.

Why spend another ten years hoping Bitcoin will finally do what you expected it to do five years ago?

I was bullish when the facts justified being bullish. The facts have changed, and so has my mind.

The only sober take I’ve heard so far about Bitcoin is the realization that it might never make a new all-time high again.
Bitcoin has existed for less than 18 years. Today it’s trading around $65,000, almost exactly where it was five years ago!

Regardless of how bullish you are, any logical person should understand that an asset with such a short history is not guaranteed to make new high.

Could Bitcoin make new highs? Of course. But you also have to consider the possibility that we’ve already seen the top. That possibility must be part of your investment decisions.
If Bitcoin represents 5%-10% of your portfolio, that’s totally fine. Maybe one day it will make new highs. But if you have 20% to 100% of your portfolio in Bitcoin, and it stays around these levels for another ten years while you keep hoping something will change, you’re royally screwed.

Not just because of the losses, but because of the enormous opportunity cost. Ten years of your life waiting for an asset to recover while countless other opportunities pass you by.

David Sacks: Jensen Huang’s Exit Is a Big Win for China

“You ask the question ‘Cui bono? Who benefits?’ It's China. China benefits from this.

Jensen's been working on GPUs for over three decades. The chips are being improved rapidly. There's a new generation of chips that come out every year.

And it's that momentum, it's the ability to tape out a brand-new chip that's several times more powerful than last year's chip, that's the real advantage.

It's Nvidia’s competitive advantage, and it's America's advantage. It's the momentum, it's the dynamism.

People get way too hung up on some chip that was state-of-the-art four years ago. That's not where the United States has the advantage. It's that we are rapidly iterating, and we keep coming up with better and more powerful chips.

Now, let's take into account what's just happened. Do you think that Nvidia is going to lose a tempo or two? Absolutely.

Nvidia’s success was based on the ability to tape out a new chip design every year, and Jensen is fundamental to that rapid progress, the same way that Elon is fundamental to the rapid progress at SpaceX or Tesla.

And if you take him out of the picture, there's just nobody comparable.

It means that Nvidia’s chips will not continue to advance at the same pace. That's really good news for Huawei because they will catch up a lot faster.”

David Friedberg: Was Jensen Taken Out So the Deep State Could Control AI?

@friedberg:

“I do worry that there is legislation coming our way with the new Congress that is going to say, ‘Every AI chip and every computer and every data center has a switch and has a connection back to some central system.’ And that central system will be a state system.

And we are fundamentally looking at an Orwellian state explosion if this sort of thing happens.

And my guess is that people know Jensen's philosophy.

Jensen has talked a lot about AI being for the benefit of all of humanity, regardless of your country, regardless of your standing, regardless of your wealth.

He was anti-oligopoly, he was the opposite of the oligarchy.

And the central state, the totalitarian state, represents everything that I believe Jensen was against.

And because of that, I think he had to be taken out if ultimately the goal is to have the totalitarian state use this technology as a tool.”
